title: Alternate names for tunes: Fidgety Feet, Tiger Rag, Tin Roof Blues
summary: Howard says Fidgety Feet and War Cloud are the same song, and talks about other names for Tiger Rag and Tin Roof Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I was going to ask. You know, let's see. I've got a month in here I had now to ask about some of the pieces, the different names of the pieces. Like the other night when you called it, Fidgety Feet, you said War Cloud.
Well yeah, well some say Fidgety Feet, some say War Cloud. But it's the same song. Yeah.
Was that an old number before the fiction? Yes, old number. I always picked it up. Was it a street march or something? Do you think it was on the marches on the street?
You could play it on the street if you want to.
I have heard it on the street. You can play it. You could play it on the street. Play it anyway. The first part has all those clarinet breaks in. I just wondered where it came from.
Well I wouldn't know that part, but I know it's a real old number. It's way back in there.
Did you all have any other names for Tiger Rag?
No, all I know was Tiger Rag.
Some people call it number two Rag and different things. No, I don't know about that.
But I know Tiger Rag.
What about Tin Roof Blues? Is that a...
Tin Roof Blues? That's all I ever know about that was Tin Roof Blues. Yes, sir. Yes, sir.
Yes, sir. Some people, I don't know what they call it, what's that name, because your water's on. Don't get funky because your water's on. Did you ever hear it called that, do you remember?
Yes. Get funky because your water's on, yes. That's the same as the Tin Roof Blues. Yes. They put a pot, put different licks in there. Yes, a little different though.
Yes, that's right. Are there any other, those old time pieces that had some crazy names like that, or some of them that you couldn't even print, you might say?
Oh, yeah.

Most of them, I mean, have... Oh, let's see, somebody, I can't think of... Oh, one of these pieces called something on the tracks or on the rail, all of a sudden. It's on a track. No, I can't think of the name. I was just wondering about some of the other, why did they have those other names for them? Did they have other words, second set of words to those songs, or did they just...
No, as I know, they're the same words. Same words.
That's why they called that water clouds, say, Pitcher Defeat, as an example. No, just some say water clouds or something.
I don't know what reason that they had that, but it's the same song.
You see?
And I said, play fidgety feet, play wall clouds, the same thing. Thanks.
